title: Rail foundation apprenticeship
introduction:
Foundation apprenticeships are employed positions and are for younger people who will benefit from a wide range of experiences. Each foundation apprenticeship provides a mix of employability skills and behaviours, technical knowledge and skills, and associated English and maths. It combines valuable hands-on practice in the workplace with off-the-job learning. The apprentice’s experiences will not only help them to grow their skills but will also help to inform their next career steps.

Completion of this foundation apprenticeship will certify achievement of all of the technical knowledge and skills, together with all of the employability skills and behaviours described. The typical progression routes will likely include employment or progression onto another skills product such as a level 2 or level 3 apprenticeship.

Foundation apprenticeships benefit employers as they get to see the apprentice in work-based settings while the apprentice receives extra support. Employers also benefit from accessing a broader talent pool of young learners than they might otherwise do. Under DfE Apprenticeship funding Rules 25/26 the employer qualifies for up to £2,000 per foundation apprentice, subject to retention and progression.
overviewOfRole: Rail foundation practitioners support the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the railway, helping to ensure customers and goods reach their destinations safely and on time.
fullOverview:
Start Your Career in Rail
 
Get Paid, Gain Skills, Build Your Future

Looking for a job where you can earn money, learn new skills and start a career with real opportunities?

As a Rail foundation apprentice, you'll be part of the team that keeps Britain's railway moving. Every day, you'll help people and goods get to where they need to go, support train services, and make a difference to millions of passengers across the country.

No two days are the same. You'll gain hands-on experience across a variety of railway environments, including stations, depots, control and signalling centres, offices and other operational sites. Working alongside experienced rail professionals, you'll develop valuable skills while contributing to the smooth running of rail services.

The broad purpose of the role is to support the safe, reliable and efficient operation of the railway, helping to ensure customers and goods reach their destinations safely and on time.

Daily duties may include:

  • Supporting operational and customer-facing activities across the railway network.
  • Assisting colleagues to deliver safe, efficient and reliable rail services.
  • Following safe systems of work and industry procedures.
  • Communicating effectively with colleagues, customers and stakeholders.
  • Helping to create a safe, comfortable and customer-focused journey for passengers.
  • Supporting the day-to-day operation of stations, depots, control centres and other rail environments.

Throughout your apprenticeship you'll earn while you learn, building practical experience, industry knowledge and transferable skills that can open the door to a range of exciting careers in rail.

This apprenticeship can provide a pathway to future opportunities including:

  • Train Driver

Driving trains safely and helping passengers or goods reach their destination on time

  • Transport Scheduler

Planning timetables and train services to keep people and goods moving.

  • Passenger Transport Operative 

Assisting customers, providing travel information and helping to keep stations running smoothly.

  • Rail Infrastructure Operative

Operating signalling and train control systems to manage the rail transport network.

  • Other operational, technical and management roles across the rail industry

Progressing into leadership, training, safety, planning or other specialist careers across the railway. 

The railway connects people, communities, and businesses across the country. This is your chance to be part of something bigger, gain valuable skills, and start building a successful future in Great British Railways.

 If you're looking for a rewarding career, enjoy working as part of a team and want to make a real difference every day, this apprenticeship is a great place to start your journey.

Earn, Learn, Succeed. Your career in rail starts here.
assessmentDetails:
This assessment plan sets out the requirements for the assessment of the level 2 Rail Foundation Apprenticeship. The assessment outcomes group and summarise the knowledge and skills that must be demonstrated in assessments and are of equal weighting. The assessment organisation must ensure that all assessment outcomes are met.

It is important that the assessment of foundation apprentices is proportionate and supports the swift progression of learners onto their next destination, whether that be a further apprenticeship, entering the workplace, or another programme of study. As such, assessment organisations must design assessments to ensure there is no unnecessary delay in the progression of learners.

This assessment plan does not prescribe when assessment takes place. Apprentices may be assessed at appropriate points (or milestones) throughout their Foundation Apprenticeship.

This assessment plan does not prescribe assessment methods, but does require:

  • a knowledge test
  • a practical assessment 

The practical assessment must give the foundation apprentice the opportunity to demonstrate the practical application of the knowledge and skills they have acquired over the course of their training. This may take many forms, including (but not limited to) observation, undertaking a set task in a simulated environment, direct assessment of materials generated during their training, projects, presentations, compiling a portfolio of evidence.

The assessment organisation must set Foundation Apprenticeship assessments. The assessment organisation may design the assessment to permit a centre to mark the assessment(s). The assessment organisation is responsible for ensuring all assessments are sufficiently reliable and valid, and the accuracy of any centre marking. Assessment organisations are permitted to sample within knowledge and skills statements, and evidence can be drawn from one or more occupations.

Assessment outcomes

(*) English and maths are important to Foundation Apprenticeships. Knowledge and skills statements which offer opportunities to develop functional English and maths are identified with an asterisk. Please see the occupational standard for further details.

Performance descriptor

 The performance descriptor for a Pass is:

Foundation apprentices must demonstrate the requirements, as set out in the occupational standard:

  • reliably
  • effectively
  • to an appropriate degree for the level of the standard 


Overall performance across the range of requirements for the foundation apprenticeship assessment is secure. 

Assessment requirements

Access to work: Health, safety, security and ethics in rail environments

AO1: Health, safety, security and ethical working in rail environments

Access to work knowledge and skills are fundamental to employment in occupations related to this Foundation Apprenticeship. These knowledge and skills are mapped to AO1. Where acquiring these knowledge and skills is required to access the workplace, this assessment should happen early in the programme.

The assessment of knowledge in AO1 must be assessment organisation set and marked. This may be in a single assessment or more than one assessment, providing there is no duplication of content. Digital assessment methods should be prioritised, where appropriate.

 

Technical Knowledge and Skills

AO2: Railway operations and customer support

AO3: Communication and teamwork

Technical knowledge and skills are areas of technical ability in related occupations. These knowledge and skills are mapped to AO2 and AO3.

AO2 describes those knowledge and skills associated with rail environments and those who work within the environments. AO3 describes the knowledge and skills specifically associated with communication and teamwork.

The assessment organisation must ensure that a foundation apprentice is assessed on AO2 and AO3. This may be in a single assessment or more than one assessment, providing there is no duplication of content.

Employability skills and behaviours

Employability skills and behaviours are highly transferable and universal across Foundation Apprenticeships. They support work-readiness. Employability skills and behaviour (EB) statements are not formally assessed. 

However, assessment organisations must confirm with employers that they have been suitably demonstrated over the course of the Foundation Apprenticeship before awarding the Foundation Apprenticeship. EB6 does not need to be confirmed by the employer but should form a key element of the apprentice’s off-the-job training package.
entryRequirements: There are no formal entry requirements (only applicable where there is an MQ or a regulatory requirement e.g. age restrictions due to health and safety).
englishAndMathsQualifications:
Functional English and maths

(*) Knowledge and skills statements which offer opportunities to develop functional English and maths are identified with an asterisk.

These are knowledge or skills statements which provide a learner with an opportunity to utilise English and maths in a workplace. This could include reading instructions, measuring or recording information.

English and maths qualifications

Apprentices must follow the English and maths formal qualification requirements as set out in the Department for Education Apprenticeship funding rules.
mandatoryQualificationsOrLicenceToPracti: There are no mandatory qualifications or licence to practice requirements for this occupation.

technicalKnowledges.detail: Fundamental principles of rail safety, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and awareness of railway hazards.
Why Safe Systems of Work, including health, safety and environmental regulations, are required within the rail industry.
Fundamental principles of equity, diversity and inclusion in the workplace and how they contribute to a psychologically safe environment.
The railway customer base and the needs of different types of customers , providing an inclusive and professional service.
Written, verbal and digital communication techniques, including safety-critical communication and structured messaging.*
Roles and responsibilities across the railway. For example, key elements of the rail system, including passenger and freight operations, track infrastructure etc.
Basic railway components and terminology to support operational awareness and effective working practices.*
Security risks and protocols, suspicious indicators, and reporting procedures. For example, Station safety checks.
Fundamental principles of self-management and self-motivation techniques, including personal responsibility for being fit for duty.
The purpose and different types of railway standards key performance indicators (KPIs), and targets.*
The purpose and basic features of railway timetables, plans and work schedules relevant to different rail operations.

How incidents and disruption are managed on the railway and how service is maintained during disruption. For example bus replacement services, crowd management, back office operational support, delay on-board trains and associated risks.
Commercial and operational interdependencies across the rail network. For example working with government and trade unions.

technicalSkills.detail: Comply with employee responsibilities under health, safety and welfare regulations.
Work in accordance with Safe Systems of Work, including health, safety and environmental requirements.
Demonstrate safety-critical communications using structured protocols for example using radios, whistles, approved phones, torches, hand and arm signals as well as the phonetic alphabet.*
Use relevant systems and provide accurate information. For example, customer information screens and specific phone apps.*
Assist customers, including those with additional requirements, in a professional and inclusive manner within the limits of own role and responsibility.
Respond to conflict professionally under supervision. For example people on the wrong train, incorrect tickets, cancelled or delayed trains.
Identify and escalate hazards, faults, and security concerns.
Support responses to railway emergencies under supervision. For example, station evacuations.*
Work as part of a railway team under supervision in line with EDI principles.
Develop personal resilience when working in a railway environment.
Prepare and organise self for work.
Demonstrate an understanding of how an activity, change or issue in one part of the railway may affect other operations, organisations or stakeholders.
Explore career and progression opportunities across the rail industry and identify own development needs and potential next steps.

employabilitySkillsAndBehaviours.detail: Communicate and share information using verbal, non-verbal, written and digital methods.
Act in a professional manner including good time keeping and conduct.
Apply new learning and feedback to everyday practice.
Complete own work tasks and ask for help when needed.
Work with colleagues to contribute to team outcomes.
Seek ways to manage own financial, health and wellbeing needs using available resources.
Overcome challenges and adapt to changes at work.
Work in line with health, safety and environmental requirements.

informationForProviders: Coverage of each knowledge and skill statement must include each and every occupation it is mapped to, unless expressly stated otherwise. For instance, if skill S1 is mapped to occupation 1 and occupation 2, then the range of coverage must include elements of both 1 and 2 so the apprentice benefits from a broad experience. Competence is to the level described by this Foundation Apprenticeship’s knowledge and skills and not the often higher level of the mapped occupations. Coverage will be a blend of on and off the job learning. Please refer to the Knowledge and skills coverage document.
